controls.text: This breaker enables engine start-up, operation and monitoring and also the 3x36 volt inverter for the engine gauges.
controls.context: It must be on for the oil, fuel and turn indicators to work.

controls.name: AGD-GMK circuit breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This breaker powers the artificial horizon and the gyro compass through the PT-500C inverter.
controls.context: Without it the attitude indicator and the radio magnetic indicator do not work.

controls.name: 115V inverter circuit breakers (1 and 2)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These two breakers switch on the two inverters that make 115 volt alternating current from the battery power. The radios and navigation sets need it.
controls.context: If one inverter fails the other takes over, and the INV. 115V FAIL light flashes.

controls.name: RDO (ICS and radio) circuit breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This breaker powers the intercom and the radio.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot switches it off during the engine start and on again after.

controls.name: MRP-RV circuit breaker (marker beacon receiver and radar altimeter)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This breaker powers the marker beacon receiver and the radar altimeter.
controls.context: A marker beacon is a small radio beacon on the ground that the plane flies over on approach.

controls.name: RSBN (ISKRA) circuit breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This breaker powers the RSBN-5S / ISKRA-K navigation system.
controls.context: After about 3 minutes the RMI and the PPD-2 show direction and distance.

controls.name: RSBN (ISKRA) emergency connection switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This switch keeps the RSBN powered from the backup generator or the battery if the main generator fails.
controls.context: It is an emergency connection.

controls.name: IFF (SRO) emergency connection switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This switch powers the IFF transponder from the battery if both generators fail.
controls.context: The IFF panel itself is not used in the game.

controls.name: WING TANKS circuit breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This breaker turns on the indication system of the fuel in the wingtip tanks.
controls.context: When the WING TIP TANKS light says they are empty, the pilot switches this breaker off.

controls.name: RIO-3 de-icing signal circuit breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This breaker powers the RIO-3 ice sensor.
controls.context: The sensor is needed for the automatic mode of the anti-icing.

controls.name: SDU circuit breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This breaker powers the SDU remote command landing system.
controls.context: The SDU also needs its own switch on the right panel.

controls.name: ARMS circuit breaker (weapon circuits power)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: This breaker gives power to the weapon control system and the combat trigger on the stick.
controls.context: The rear cockpit has its own ARMS breaker, which overrides the one in the front.

controls.name: Heating AOA sensor circuit breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: The game names this breaker 'CB Heating AOA Sensor Switch'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: AOA means angle of attack: how steeply the wing meets the air.

controls.name: Main CB panel
controls.text: This is the whole main breaker panel of the front cockpit. The breakers are described one by one in this panel.
controls.context: The manual lists 15 breakers here. The switches act as switches and breakers at once.

panels.name: Auxiliary CB panel
panels.text: This panel has 24 more circuit breakers. They power the lights, the engine start panel, the pitot heaters and several other systems. In normal use the ground crew switches them all on.
panels.context: In the game all auxiliary breakers are on at the start. The pilot only checks that they are on.

controls.name: Auxiliary CB panel
controls.text: This is the whole auxiliary breaker panel of the front cockpit. The breakers are described in groups in this panel.
controls.context: The manual lists 24 breakers on it.

controls.name: Air conditioning and de-icing breakers (2)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: AIR COND and ANTI-ICE (DEICING AIR SHOWER).
controls.context: They supply the air conditioning and the anti-icing system. The manual says the ventilation suit part is not implemented.

controls.name: Pitot heater breakers (left and right)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: PITOT LEFT (stand-by) and PITOT RIGHT (main).
controls.context: They power the heaters of the standby (left) and the main (right) pitot tube.

controls.name: PT-500C and engine instrument breakers (2)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: PT-500C and ENGINE INSTRUMENTS.
controls.context: The PT-500C breaker enables the inverter for the artificial horizon and the compass. The engine instruments breaker enables the SPT-40 inverter for the engine gauges.

controls.name: ARC (ADF) and SRO (IFF) breakers (2)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: ARC and SRO.
controls.context: They power the RKL-41 automatic direction finder and the SRO-2M IFF transponder. The IFF panel is not used in the game.

controls.name: SEAT-HELMET breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: SEAT-HELMET.
controls.context: It supplies the seat height adjustment and the helmet visor heating. The manual says it is not implemented in the game.

controls.name: RT-12 JPT regulator power breaker

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: RT-12 JPT REG.
controls.context: It powers the engine overheat protection. The game calls it the RT-12 JPT regulator power switch.

controls.name: Gears, control and signalling breakers (3)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: GEARS (U/C BALANCE), CONTROL (CONTR.) and SIGNALING (SIGN.).
controls.context: They supply the landing gear, flap and trimmer controls and indication, the flap and air brake control with the critical Mach indication, and the indicator lamps of the front cockpit.

controls.name: Light breakers (5)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: NAV. LIGHTS, SPOTLIGHT LEFT, SPOTLIGHT RIGHT, RED LIGHTS and WHITE LIGHTS.
controls.context: They supply the exterior lights, the landing and taxi lights and the red and white cockpit lights.

controls.name: Starting panel, booster pump and ignition breakers (4)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: START PANEL, BOOSTER PUMP, IGNITION 1 and IGNITION 2.
controls.context: They supply the engine starting panel, the fuel pump of the engine and the ignition that is needed for the engine start, running and monitoring.

controls.name: Fire, emergency jettison and recorder breakers (3)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The circuit breaker is on and the system has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The circuit breaker is off and the system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: FIRE, EMERGENCY JETTISON and SARPP.
controls.context: They supply the fire extinguishing system, the emergency jettison switch, and the signal flare launcher, the ejection system and the flight data recorder.

panels.name: Center pedestal: fire warning test
panels.text: The center pedestal under the instrument panel holds the switch that tests the fire warning system.
panels.context: The pilot tests the fire detection before each flight.

controls.name: Fire warning signal test switch (TEST SSP: I / OFF / II)

positions.name: I
positions.text: Tests the first group of fire sensors.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: Normal position.

positions.name: II
positions.text: Tests the second group of fire sensors.

controls.text: This switch tests the two groups of fire sensors. It springs back to the middle.
controls.context: The manual says: hold it at I, the FIRE warning light must light, release it, then do the same at II. This only proves that both channels work electrically.

areas.name: Stick, throttle and pedals (front)
areas.text: The stick is in the middle between the knees, the throttle is on the left console and the pedals are on the floor.

panels.name: Control stick (front cockpit)
panels.text: The control stick in the middle between the pilot's knees steers the plane up, down, left and right. The L-39 has mechanical controls: the stick is connected to the elevator and ailerons by rods.
panels.context: The front stick has the combat trigger and the buttons for the trimmers, the brakes and the gun camera. The rear stick has fewer buttons.

controls.name: Control stick (pitch and roll)
controls.text: Pushing the stick forward points the nose down and pulling it back points the nose up. Moving it sideways rolls the plane.
controls.context: The stick works the elevator and the ailerons through rods. There are no hydraulics in this control line.

controls.name: Stick part 'RUS'
controls.text: The game lists the stick body in its device view under the name 'RUS'. The manual does not describe this part separately.
controls.context: The control stick itself is described in its own entry.

controls.name: Trimmer button (elevator and aileron trim)
controls.text: This four-way button on top of the grip moves the neutral point of the stick. Up and down trim the nose, left and right trim the wing.
controls.context: Trim lets the pilot fly straight without holding the stick. The elevator trimmer must not be used above 700 km per hour. A neutral position indicator is on the centre console.

controls.name: Combat trigger
controls.text: This trigger fires the weapon that was chosen on the armament panel: bombs, rockets, missiles or guns. It is on the front stick only.
controls.context: It works only if the armament breakers are on and the speed is above 310 km per hour.

controls.name: Combat trigger safety cover
controls.text: This small cover over the trigger prevents it from being pressed by accident. The pilot lifts it before an attack.
controls.context: In the game the cover is opened and closed with a key press.

controls.name: Wheel brake lever
controls.text: Pressing this lever on the front of the grip brakes both main wheels at the same time. Letting go releases the brakes.
controls.context: Together with the rudder pedals it also brakes one side more than the other, to turn on the ground. The rear stick has its own lever, which overrides the front one.

controls.name: FKP gun camera button
controls.text: Pressing this button checks that the gun camera works.
controls.context: The camera itself takes pictures when the combat trigger is pressed.

panels.name: Throttle (front cockpit)
panels.text: The throttle handle on the left console sets the engine power, like the gas pedal of a car. The handle has buttons for the air brakes, the radio and the intercom, and a twist grip for the gunsight range.
panels.context: The throttle in the front cockpit has the STOP latch and the markings of the engine modes. The rear throttle has a lock instead, so the engine can only be stopped from the front.

controls.name: Throttle handle
controls.text: Moving the handle forward gives the engine more power, moving it back gives less. STOP, IDLE, CR SPEED, NOM and TAKE OFF are marked.
controls.context: The engine has no afterburner. TAKE OFF is the strongest setting. The pilot starts the engine with the throttle at STOP and then moves it to IDLE.

controls.name: STOP latch
controls.text: This latch at the rear of the throttle's travel must be pulled to move the throttle from IDLE back to STOP, which stops the engine.
controls.context: It stops the throttle from slipping into STOP by accident. The front throttle is the only one with a latch.

controls.name: Air brake switch

positions.name: RETRACT
positions.text: The air brakes close (switch forward).

positions.name: EXTEND
positions.text: The air brakes open (switch aft).

controls.text: This switch on the throttle opens and closes the air brakes, the panels that open into the wind to slow the plane down. Pressing it in like a button opens them for a short time.
controls.context: The air brakes open by themselves at about Mach 0.78. The AIR BRAKE OUT lamp shows they are out.

controls.name: RADIO button
controls.text: While this button is held, the pilot talks on the radio. It is the push-to-talk button.
controls.context: The radio panel on the left console picks the channel.

controls.name: SPU intercom button
controls.text: While this button is held, the pilot talks to the other cockpit over the intercom.
controls.context: The rear stick has an intercom button as well.

controls.name: Gunsight range grip (twist)
controls.text: Twisting the grip of the throttle handle sets the target distance in the gunsight. Clockwise raises it, counter-clockwise lowers it.
controls.context: The sight's range runs from 180 to 800 metres. Turning to the minimum puts the sight in FIXED mode and the maximum puts it back in GYRO.

controls.name: Throttle part 'Details'
controls.text: The game lists a part of the throttle under the name 'Details'. The manual does not describe this part.
controls.context: It has no known function in the game.

controls.name: Second throttle part 'Details'
controls.text: The game lists a second part of the throttle under the name 'Details'. The manual does not describe this part.
controls.context: It has no known function in the game.

panels.name: Rudder pedals
panels.text: The two pedals on the floor steer the rudder, the flap on the tail that turns the nose left and right. The pedals are joined to the rudder with rods.
panels.context: The pedals also work the differential brakes together with the brake lever on the stick. The pedal adjustment is not used in the game.

controls.name: Rudder pedal
controls.text: Pushing the left pedal turns the nose left and pushing the right pedal turns it right.
controls.context: The game does not show a separate callout for the pedals in the cockpit.
